records.deidentified_narrative: on thursday, june 29, 2023, i, officer m. delossantos was working patrol duty for the ingleside police department in san patricio county, texas. on this date at approximately [roadway] for an accident involving a vehicle striking a pedestrian. dispatch advised the vehicle that struck the pedestrian was still on scene and ems was in route. i arrived on scene and contacted security personal, roy flores (dob [date]), and alberto rodriguez (dob [date]) who was a witness to the scene at the security building. security personnel advised me that they were going to take me to the area where the incident occurred at. i arrived at the parking lot entrance near the administrative building where the accident occurred along with security, roy, and alberto. alberto advised that he was walking west in the roadway along the barriers inside of the parking lot with a male who was later identified as sabas herrera (dob [date]). alberto said that he was approaching the entrance to the parking lot with sabas and crossed an unmarked crosswalk to get to the other side of the roadway. alberto said as they were crossing sabas was in front of him walking and saw a vehicle make a wide left turn to come into the parking lot. alberto said when the vehicle came into the parking lot it struck sabas with the front passenger side bumper of the vehicle. alberto said sabas then fell to the ground and got back up. alberto advised the vehicle then drove off and parked in a parking spot. alberto advised the driver, later identified as enoc velasquez (dob [date]) came back to the entrance to see if sabas was okay. alberto told me he believed enoc might had been distracted while he was driving but was not entirely sure. alberto also advised that enoc was driving at a high rate of speed when he was coming into the parking lot. i then provided alberto with my business card and the [case id] for the incident. i then left and went back to the security building to contact sabas. i arrived at the security office and contacted sabas regarding the incident. sabas only spoke spanish, roy also spoke spanish, so he was translating on behalf of sabas. roy told me sabas advised he was walking west where the incident occurred at and crossed the unmarked crosswalk at the parking lot entrance to get to the other side. sabas said as he was walking, he saw a headlight from a vehicle approaching him, then got hit from the front passenger side of the vehicle. roy told me that sabas stated that roy was not driving at a high rate of speed when he turned into the parking lot. roy advised that enoc, the driver of the vehicle that hit sabas then parked his vehicle and came back to the scene to check on sabas. roy advised that sabas was checked out from ems, and he stated that he was okay and was going to report back to work. i then provided sabas with my business card and the [case id] for the incident. i then went inside the administrative building and contacted enoc about the incident. enoc advised that he was traveling west on the roadway in front of the administrative building approaching the parking lot entrance. enoc said he then proceeded to turn left into the parking lot and did not see anyone or anything on the roadway. enoc said as he was turning, he then saw a green backpack in front of him and immediately stopped his vehicle to see what he hit. enoc said he then saw sabas get up from the ground and walk away from the scene. enoc advised sabas to remain on scene until security arrived. enoc told me he checked to see if sabas was okay and never left the scene. i then went with enoc to his vehicle so i could get the license plate. i provided the license plate (tx lp jzw 6925) to dispatch. dispatch advised the vehicle came back to a 2008 black volkswagen passat. that vehicle was the car that struck sabas. i then provided enoc with my business card and the [case id] for the incident.

records.deidentified_narrative: while on patrol in full uniform and marked patrol unit police responded to listed location for a traffic crash. upon my arrival i contacted unit2's driver, who stated she was traveling east bound at the [roadway] when she observed unit1 who was traveling west bound at the 7100 block prue lose control of their vehicle and jump the center median traveling [roadway]. unit2 to avoid a head on collision with unit1, unit2 pulled to the left and jump onto the raised center median and struck a light post located in the center median. the light post fell and struck unit3 that was behind unit2. unit1 just drove around unit2 and unit3 without stopping fleeing the location. i contacted unit3's driver, who stated she was traveling east bound at the [roadway] behind unit2. unit3 witnessed unit1 who was [roadway] jump the center median and began driving on [roadway] traveling head on towards unit2 when unit2 pulled left jumping the center median striking a light post to avoid a head on collision. the light post fell down striking her vehicle causing listed damage. unit1 just drove past them on [roadway] without stopping. unit1 fled the location without rendering aide or exchanging information. ofcr. a. munoz #0756 made contact with a witness at the scene, who stated he was on the east bound side walk riding his scooter west bound when he heard unit1 jump the center median. the witness observed unit1 coming straight at him so he planted his right leg in the ground as he was moving and jump over to his left into the grass. in doing so the witness injured his leg causing minor pain, no ems needed. the witness then got on his scooter and followed unit1 who turned left down the 7100 block of shady elms. the witness was able to flag unit1 down and contact the driver. the witness told unit1's driver, you just caused a crash. unit1's driver replied that she has no damage to her car. the witness told unit1's driver she need to return. i was advised that unit1's driver returned but just continued [roadway] without contacting any drivers. the witnesses stated the unit1's driver was a white female 30-40 years of age in pink scrubs. the witness identified himself to us a retired trooper. i relocated to unit1's listed registered address but listed vehicle was not there and there was no answer at the door. i returned to the crash scene. unit3 had to be towed due to the damage, unit2 drove away on it's own power. cps made our location to disassemble the fall-in light post and secure the living electrical wires. a failure to stop and render aid-moving trc 550. 021 offense report was also generated. no further action taken. coban/bwc activated. on [date] det. c. pawelek #2131 created a supplement to crash report to add unit 1 driver's information. i also added unit 4 who was a pedestrian on the southbound side sidewalk. unit 4 [roadway] to [medical facility] and suffered a sprained knee. unit 1 driver was at fault for the crash and fled from the crash scene. unit 1 driver faces charges of failure to stop and render aid- moving, and failure to stop and provide information $200 or more.

records.deidentified_narrative: on monday, july 14th, 2023, at approximately 2123 hours, i, officer david velasco #157 was on duty wearing our police uniform, police duty gear, and driving police patrol unit #4037. my body worn camera was activated throughout this investigation. police responded to [roadway], san marcos, tx, 78666 for major accident involving a vehicle and a pedestrian. upon arrival, i observed emergency medical services (ems) attending to the pedestrian that was hit by the vehicle, [medical facility] for further evaluation. i spoke to blackwell (unit 1). she informed me that she turned into the shell gas station and was not able to come to a complete stop when she saw a pedestrian on the sidewalk. she stated that she was not able to react until her vehicle contacted the pedestrian. she informed me that the pedestrian landed on the hood of her vehicle. blackwell parked her vehicle and waited for ems and pd to arrive on scene. i was provided two separate witness statements for this incident; they are as follow:witness #1: melvin informed me that he witnessed [roadway]. he stated that the pedestrian that was struck was riding [roadway]. unit one failed to see the pedestrian in time and turned into the gas station striking the pedestrian. witness #2: carlos informed me that he was sitting in the parking lot when he witnessed the incident. he stated that the pedestrian was riding his skateboard on the sidewalk going down the hill at a fast speed. he observed unit one turn into the gas station striking the pedestrian. the information provided to me has led me to conclude in my professional opinion that unit one caused the accident. unit one failed to yield the right of way to the pedestrian and was unable to control its speed leading to the vehicle striking the pedestrian. report generated under [case id]
